description: Two gals, one rover, and a bunch of suspiciously evil tardigrades. Armed with lab coats, electronics, computers and questionable scientific decisions. We will be making a mixed reality, not entirely historically accurate game about the greatest battle of the universe.
summary:
Terrorigrades is a story-driven educational arcade game that brings the history of space exploration hardware to life through an unexpected adventure on Mars.

When mysterious signals begin arriving from the supposedly inactive Opportunity rover, a new exploration rover - Serenity, is sent to investigate. What begins as a routine mission quickly turns into an extraordinary adventure involving mutated tardigrades, a mysterious hive mind and the abandoned machines of previous space missions.

Players explore Mars, encounter historical rovers, restore their functionality and uncover the scientific discoveries, instruments and stories behind real space exploration missions.

By combining retro arcade gameplay, humour, science fiction and factual educational content, Terrorigrades transforms the often-overlooked legacy of space exploration hardware into an engaging experience for casual space enthusiasts of any age.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

Terrorigrades is a browser-based, story-driven educational game set on Mars. Players take the role of Serenity, a newly deployed exploration rover sent to investigate unexpected signals originating from Opportunity, a rover that had long been considered inactive.

Upon arriving on Mars, players discover that something unusual has happened. Opportunity has developed a consciousness after being exposed to a mysterious alien hive mind, and mutated tardigrades have taken over the planet.

As the story progresses, players explore the Martian environment, encounter abandoned exploration rovers and help restore them to working condition. Each encounter introduces a real space exploration mission, its hardware, scientific instruments, discoveries and historical significance.

Educational information is integrated into the narrative and gameplay, allowing players to learn through exploration rather than traditional lessons.

What are the benefits and intended impact?

Space exploration leaves behind an extraordinary collection of technological artifacts, many of which are rarely discussed outside specialist educational materials.

Our project aims to make these artifacts interesting and accessible to space fans of any age.

By presenting real missions through fictional characters and interactive storytelling, we hope to encourage curiosity (pun intended) about planetary exploration, biology, robotics, engineering and scientific discovery. We also want players to appreciate that even missions that have ended continue to contribute to our understanding of the Solar System.

Tools and technologies

The project combines a browser-based game with a physical electronics prototype.

  • Software: A web-based game developed using AI-assisted coding tools.
  • Hardware: An Arduino-based rover prototype, constructed using a handmade cardboard chassis and electronic components.
  • Physical prototyping: Basic electronics, motor control and LED lighting.

The physical rover represents Serenity, connecting the fictional protagonist with a tangible engineering project and demonstrating how the concept can extend beyond the screen. Just look at her, how could you not love her?

Creativity and design considerations

Our main creative approach was to combine an unconventional science-fiction story with the visual language of retro 16-bit arcade games.

Instead of presenting historical rovers as static objects or entries in a timeline, we give them personalities and integrate their real missions into the player's progression. Repairing and recovering these machines becomes a way of discovering their actual history and scientific contributions.

We deliberately chose humour, unusual characters and an exaggerated storyline to make scientific information less intimidating and more memorable.

Throughout development, we considered accessibility for casual players, the balance between entertainment and scientific accuracy, and the importance of making the educational content relevant to the actual hardware and missions being represented.
